# Clalit Health (clalit-mcp)

Read the user's own Clalit e-services records. Unofficial. Read-only.

Use the CLI when you can run shell commands on the **user's machine** with a normal residential network. Clalit sits behind Imperva; datacenter and cloud agent hosts usually get Error 16 and cannot log in.

## Setup (checkout)

```sh
git clone https://github.com/netanelavr/clalit-mcp.git
cd clalit-mcp
npm install
npm test
```

Every command below is run from the repo root:

```sh
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts help
```

`npx skills add netanelavr/clalit-mcp` installs this skill for Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, and other agents that support skills.

## Login

The user must solve the portal CAPTCHA and enter the SMS OTP in a loopback browser page. Nothing is solved automatically.

```sh
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts login
```

Session cookies are stored at `~/.config/clalit-mcp/session.json` (mode `0600`). Never commit or paste that file.

ID, CAPTCHA, and OTP may appear in the conversation when the user provides them — that is how interactive login works.

## Reads (after login)

Use `--json` for machine-readable output.

```sh
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts labs --json
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts lab --ref TOKEN --json
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts lab-document --ref TOKEN --out /tmp/clalit-lab.pdf
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts prescriptions --json
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts prescription-status --prescription NO --medication ID --form NAME --start DATE --section ID --json
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts lab-orders --json
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts lab-order --ref TOKEN --json
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts documents --source visit_summaries --json   # hospital_summaries | medical_approvals | form17
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts document --ref TOKEN --out /tmp/clalit-doc.pdf
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts records --source diagnoses --json   # sensitivities | chronic_medications | medicines_purchased | medication_approvals | imaging_clinics | imaging_hospitals | imaging_external | hospital_visits | hospital_labs | referrals | appointments | recommendations | vaccinations | blood_type
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts record-document --ref TOKEN --out /tmp/clalit-report.pdf
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts export --out DIR      # everything above into one folder, with a README for you to read first
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts refresh-session
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts logout
```

Take `ref` and prescription row fields from list output. Do not invent tokens.

When the user wants their whole history, a copy to keep, or many results at once, run `export` once and read the
folder (its `README.md` first) instead of calling `lab` per result: one sign-in covers everything, and the folder
outlives the session.

Exit codes: `0` success, `1` operation failure, `2` usage, `3` login / Imperva block.

## MCP

Only when clalit-mcp MCP tools are already configured in the host. From a checkout, stdio MCP:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "clalit-mcp": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["tsx", "packages/cli/src/main.ts", "mcp"],
      "cwd": "/absolute/path/to/clalit-mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

Tools: `list_labs`, `get_lab_result`, `get_lab_document`, `list_prescriptions`, `get_prescription_issue_status`, `list_lab_orders`, `get_lab_order`, `list_documents`, `get_document`, `list_records`, `get_record_document`, `get_hospital_lab_result`, plus `clalit_login`, `clalit_session_status` and `clalit_logout`.

When a tool says nobody is signed in, call `clalit_login` and give the user the link it returns. The user signs in on that page; with MCP, never ask for the ID, CAPTCHA or SMS code in the chat. The server keeps the session alive while it runs, until the length the user picked on the page.

## Privacy

Every record is real medical data. Anything you send to a model becomes part of that model's context.

Never paste ID numbers, cookies, session files, SMS codes, captcha images, lab PDFs, or HAR files into GitHub issues. Prefer a PR with a **sanitized** HTML fixture.

Security: see the repo [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/netanelavr/clalit-mcp/blob/main/SECURITY.md).

# Clalit Health

**Read your own Clalit records (lab results, prescriptions, lab orders) from a CLI or an AI assistant (MCP).**

[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

> Unofficial. Not affiliated with Clalit. Not a substitute for the official portal or clinical advice.

The MCP server runs locally on your machine: you log in through your own browser, the session is stored only on your computer, and this project has no hosted backend and collects nothing. Note that whatever results your AI client (such as Claude) requests are passed to that client and are handled under its provider's privacy terms.

![Ask Claude about your own Clalit records (read-only)](docs/assets/chat-demo.png)

## Getting started with an AI assistant

Copy and paste this to your agent:

```
Read my Clalit lab results from the last year and summarize anything out of range, then list my active prescriptions.

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/netanelavr/clalit-mcp/main/skills/clalit-mcp/SKILL.md
```

Or install the skill locally:

```sh
npx skills add netanelavr/clalit-mcp
```

## Terms of use

- **Own account only.** Never use this against someone else's record.
- **Read-only.** No booking, payments, profile writes, or prescription requests.
- **No CAPTCHA / bot / Imperva bypass.** You solve CAPTCHA and enter the SMS OTP yourself.
- **Residential machine.** Datacenter and many cloud IPs get Imperva Error 16; log in on your own Mac / home network.
- **Session file is secret.** Stored mode `0600` under `~/.config/clalit-mcp/`. Never commit or paste it.

## Install

```sh
git clone https://github.com/netanelavr/clalit-mcp.git
cd clalit-mcp
npm install
npm test
```

## Sign in and CLI

```sh
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts login
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts labs --json
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts lab --ref <token-from-labs> --json
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts lab-document --ref <token> --out result.pdf
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts prescriptions --json
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts lab-orders --json
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts lab-order --ref <token-from-lab-orders> --json
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts documents --source visit_summaries --json   # or hospital_summaries | medical_approvals | form17
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts document --ref <token-from-documents> --out summary.pdf
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts records --source diagnoses --json         # sensitivities | chronic_medications | medicines_purchased | medication_approvals | imaging_clinics | imaging_hospitals | imaging_external | hospital_visits | hospital_labs | referrals | appointments | recommendations | vaccinations | blood_type
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts hospital-lab-result --link <link-from-hospital_labs-row> --hospital <its-context.value> --json
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts record-document --ref <token-from-records> --out report.pdf
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts export --out ~/health
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts help
```

`login` opens a loopback browser page for ID, CAPTCHA, and SMS OTP. See [docs/LIVE-VERIFY.md](docs/LIVE-VERIFY.md). `login --browser` opens your own Chrome at Clalit Online's sign-in page instead: sign in there as you usually do — with your permanent password if you have one, so no SMS — and the signed-in cookies become the session ([docs/AUTH.md](docs/AUTH.md)).

## Keep a copy of everything: `export`

```sh
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts export                 # ./clalit-export-<today>/: labs (every result and its PDF), prescriptions, lab orders, documents, records
npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts export --out ~/health  # under that directory; --no-documents skips the PDFs
```

One folder: labs (one JSON per result, plus its PDF), prescriptions, lab orders, documents (visit summaries, hospital
summaries, medical approvals and Form 17 — a list and the PDFs per source), records (diagnoses, sensitivities, the
regular-medication list, pharmacy purchases, medication approvals, imaging reports with their PDFs, hospital visits and
labs with every draw's results, referrals with their PDFs, upcoming appointments, the portal's own recommendations,
vaccinations, blood type), and a root `README.md` that describes each folder for an AI assistant (layout in [docs/CLI.md](docs/CLI.md)). `--from`/`--to` (`dd.MM.yyyy`) filter labs only, default 01.01.1990 to today; a rerun skips what it already has.
Layout modeled on [Health Records Export for Maccabi](https://github.com/RoniRachmani/health-records-export-for-maccabi); [liberate-labs](https://github.com/Urigo/liberate-labs) can load it into SQLite.
The folder is not encrypted, and anything you open in an AI app is sent to that provider (see the privacy note at the top).

## MCP

Sign in first (`login` above); the MCP server reuses that local session.

### Claude Desktop

Edit `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json` (macOS). Use **absolute paths** (Dock-launched Claude does not see `nvm` / shell `PATH`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "clalit": {
      "command": "/absolute/path/to/node",
      "args": [
        "/absolute/path/to/clalit-mcp/node_modules/.bin/tsx",
        "/absolute/path/to/clalit-mcp/packages/cli/src/main.ts",
        "mcp"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Find your node path with `which node`. Quit Claude fully (Cmd+Q) and reopen.

![Claude Desktop: seven Clalit tools](docs/assets/connectors.png)

### Other MCP clients (Cursor, Claude Code, …)

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "clalit": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["tsx", "packages/cli/src/main.ts", "mcp"],
      "cwd": "/absolute/path/to/clalit-mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

### Signing in from the assistant

A session made with `login` is picked up. Without one, the tools answer with a link to a sign-in page the server serves itself on `http://localhost:8765/` (`clalit_login` returns the same link): open it, pick how long to stay signed in (1 hour to 1 week), and enter the ID, the CAPTCHA and the SMS code there — only ever on that page, never in the chat. While the server runs it keeps the session alive and signs out at the end of the length you picked ([docs/MCP.md](docs/MCP.md)).

### Tools

| Tool | What it reads |
| --- | --- |
| `list_labs`, `get_lab_result`, `get_lab_document` | Lab history, one result, the original lab PDF |
| `list_prescriptions`, `get_prescription_issue_status` | Prescriptions and their pharmacy issue status |
| `list_lab_orders`, `get_lab_order` | Lab orders and one order's detail |
| `list_documents`, `get_document` | Visit summaries, hospital summaries, medical approvals, Form 17, and their PDFs |
| `list_records`, `get_record_document`, `get_hospital_lab_result` | Diagnoses, sensitivities, chronic medications, purchased medicines, medication approvals, imaging reports (clinics, hospitals, external) with their PDFs, hospital visits, hospital labs and their result pages, referrals with their PDFs, upcoming appointments, the portal's recommendations, vaccinations, blood type |
| `clalit_login`, `clalit_session_status`, `clalit_logout` | The sign-in link, whether a session is live and until when, and sign-out |

## Mapping the portal: `tools/sitemap.mts`

```sh
npx tsx tools/sitemap.mts --out ./clalit-sitemap          # sitemap.json: which pages your account has and what they are made of
npx tsx tools/sitemap.mts --out ./clalit-sitemap --raw    # also keeps each page's HTML under raw/ (private) for writing parsers
```

A GET-only, paced walk over the signed-in portal's own links. `sitemap.json` records titles, headings, form field names,
dropdown labels and grid headers — never a value — so a page nobody reads yet can be turned into a reader from evidence.
The record sources above were built from one such map.

# Changelog

## 2026-11-02

- **Documents**: `documents` / `document` (CLI) and `list_documents` / `get_document` (MCP) read visit summaries (סיכומי ביקור רפואה יועצת), hospital summaries (סיכומים מבתי חולים, searched per hospital), medical approvals (אישורים רפואיים) and Form 17 (התחייבויות) with their PDFs; a search that fills the portal's 10-row page is split by date until every row is found. Ported from [tadnir/clalit-mcp](https://github.com/tadnir/clalit-mcp) by Michael Tadnir.
- **Records**: `records --source` / `record-document` (CLI) and `list_records` / `get_record_document` (MCP) read the portal's grid pages as they are shown, keyed by their Hebrew headers: diagnoses, sensitivities, chronic medications, medicines purchased (since 08.2008, pager walked), medication approvals, imaging reports from clinics, Clalit hospitals and external institutes (with the report PDF), hospital visits, hospital labs (with every draw's result page, read with the lab-detail parser), general referrals (last year only, with the PDF) — the page the roadmap had as "blocked" — plus upcoming appointments (home page), the portal's personalised recommendations (Measures), and vaccinations and blood type from the endpoints the portal's React pages read. Built from a `tools/sitemap.mts` map of a live account and `tools/dump-page.mts` dumps of its pages and bundles.
- **`export`**: the document and record sources too — `documents/<source>/` and `records/<source>/` with `list.json` and `files/*.pdf`; `--no-documents` skips every PDF and keeps the lists.
- **Session**: a saved session now records its last use (`lastUsedAt`), so a fresh process measures idleness from there and not from the sign-in — a session a keep-alive had held for 30+ minutes was being refused.
- **`keep-alive`** (CLI): holds the session open from a second terminal while `export` or the sitemap runs; the portal drops an idle session after ~10 minutes.
- **MCP server**: sign-in and keep-alive live in the server. The keeper ends a session only when the portal demands a sign-in (`ReauthenticationRequired`); a network error or an Imperva hiccup while opening or checking a saved session keeps `session.json` and retries on the next round, and `checkSession()` reports a 5xx as a retryable `UpstreamError`, not a sign-out. `clalit_login` returns a link to a sign-in page the server serves on `localhost:8765` (ID, CAPTCHA and SMS code are typed there, never in the chat, with a chosen session length of 1 hour to 1 week); the session is kept alive with `RefreshSession.aspx` while the server runs; `clalit_session_status`, `clalit_logout`. A session from the CLI is shared. Also from tadnir/clalit-mcp. The `login` pages use relative links, so they also work behind a path prefix ([docs/HOSTING.md](docs/HOSTING.md)).
- **`tools/sitemap.mts`**: a GET-only, paced walk over the signed-in portal that records which pages an account has and their shapes (titles, form field names, dropdown labels, grid headers — never a value), for building new readers from evidence; `--raw` keeps the HTML privately.

## 2026-10-22

- **`export`**: a lab result the portal offers no PDF for is skipped (counted in the README), no longer filed in `export-errors.json`; on a first run it costs no request. `NO_DOCUMENT` has a message of its own.
- **`login --browser`**: sign in in your own Chrome (permanent password or SMS; CAPTCHA by hand) and hand the signed-in cookies to the CLI, checked with one labs-list request before `session.json` is written; the browser's user agent stays with the session. `--keep-open` leaves the window open after the CLI exits. `--record` writes a value-free record of the sign-in's request shapes for building a browserless sign-in.

## 2026-10-21

- **`export`**: everything the client reads into one folder — labs (every result and its PDF), prescriptions, lab orders — with a `README.md` data dictionary for assistants, `export-errors.json`, `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md`; paced, resumable into the same folder, stops cleanly on an ended session. Layout modeled on Health Records Export for Maccabi.
- **Labs parsers read the live pages.** `LabsTestList.aspx` rows are date | lab section | referring doctor | test number | "הצגה": the section is now the row's name (it was the link's text) and `doctor`/`testNumber` are kept. `LabTestDetails.aspx` is read from its real grid (`tr[trtype=labData]`): one analyte per row with the shown `result`, its leading `value`, `units` or a `qualifier` (Negative), the reference range from the bar (`referenceRange`, `rangeMin`, `rangeMax`), a `flag` (L/H) computed as the page's own script does, `turnaround`, Clalit's `explanation`, and the opaque `compare` link; the lab's remarks become `notes`; microbiology results come from their own grid; the sample's `date`/`time` and the `testNumber` are read from the header, the member's name and ID are not. The old column heuristic had read the range bar's numbers as rows and the explanation's close button as units. Fixtures are now the live layouts (redacted captures), plus `lab-detail-micro.html`.

# Contributing

Never commit HAR files, cookies, session exports, ID numbers, or real lab PDFs. Prefer sanitized HTML fixtures under `packages/core/test/fixtures/`. Do not invent portal endpoints — extend only what [API sources](docs/API-SOURCES.md) documents, with matching fixtures.

```sh
npm install
npm run check
```

Keep the private-core → CLI → MCP layout. Do not document `@clalit/core` as a public SDK.

Add CHANGELOG entries under a dated `## YYYY-MM-DD` heading (the merge date), never `## Unreleased`.

# Security

## Reporting

Do **not** open a public issue for vulnerabilities that could expose medical records, session cookies, or authentication weaknesses.

Email the maintainer via GitHub: https://github.com/netanelavr — use a private advisory if available on this repository (`Security` → `Report a vulnerability`).

Include:

- Description and impact
- Reproduction **without** real PHI, real cookies, or full HAR dumps
- Sanitized HTML snippets or redacted maps only

## Project rules

- No CAPTCHA, Imperva, or SMS OTP bypass code will be accepted.
- No commits of `*.har`, cookies, `session.json`, or personal lab PDFs.
- Own-account reads only; family-member switching is out of scope and refused.

# API sources

Evidence from **redacted HAR notes** (path and field **names** only; raw HARs are never committed). Status: partial pass from captured traffic plus later live HTML checks. Prescriptions and lab orders follow the same process.

## Surface

- ASP.NET WebForms (`__VIEWSTATE` / `__EVENTVALIDATION` / `__doPostBack`)
- Mostly `text/html`
- Labs PDF via POST returning `application/octet-stream`
- Prescriptions issue status via JSON POST (read status only)

## Hosts

- `e-services.clalit.co.il` (primary)
- `accessibility.clalit.co.il` (allowlisted; not required for MVP reads)

## Owner scope

- Family switch controls exist in HTML (`FamilySliderControl21$au`, `FamilySliderControl21$cu`). **MVP rule:** never set family switch; only follow detail links from the authenticated owner's own list pages.

## Labs

| Operation | Method / path |
| --- | --- |
| List | `GET /OnlineWeb/Services/Labs/LabsTestList.aspx` |
| Date fields | `ctl00$ctl00$cphBody$bodyContent$LabsHistory1$datepickerRangeCalendar$txtFromDate` / `$txtToDate` |
| Grid | `LabsHistory1$gvTestListInDateRange` (pager/sort via `__doPostBack`) |
| Detail | `GET /OnlineWeb/Services/Labs/LabTestDetails.aspx` query `s`, `d`, `ls` |
| Document | `POST` same detail page with `__EVENTTARGET` (left-menu download control) → `application/octet-stream` PDF |

## Prescriptions (מרשמים)

| Operation | Method / path |
| --- | --- |
| List | `GET /OnlineWeb/Services/Medicine/PatientPrescriptionsex.aspx` |
| Date / filter fields | `dateRange$txtFromDate` / `$txtToDate`, `chkIncludeExpiredPrescriptions`, `hdnSectionID` |
| Repeaters | `rptPatientPrescriptions$ctlNN` → nested `rptMedicine$ctlNN` |
| Row `data-*` | `data-prescription`, `data-medicineId`, `data-medicineFormName`, `data-medicineStartDate` |
| Issue status (read) | `POST /onlineweb/api/PatientPrescriptions/IssueDrugsByPatientReceiptId` |
| Issue request keys | `prescriptionNo`, `medicationID`, `medicationFormName`, `medicationStartDate`, `sectionId`, `currStatusValue` |

# Authentication

## Upstream flow (observed, redacted endpoint map)

Host: `https://e-services.clalit.co.il`

1. `POST /onlineweb/general/infootplogin.aspx`  
   Live fields (2026-09): `ctl00$cphBody$tbUserId`, `ctl00$cphBody$tbCaptchaLogin`, BotDetect `LBD_VCID_…` (hidden instance id; image query uses `t=`), `__EVENTTARGET=ctl00$cphBody$btnSendOTP` (LinkButton, not a type=submit), plus `__VIEWSTATE` / `__EVENTVALIDATION`. Older `BDC_VCID_*` + `btnLogin` submit shapes are still accepted when present.
2. `GET/POST /OnlineWeb/General/OTPSMSVerification.aspx`  
   Field `ctl00$cphBody$txtClientOTP`, plus hidden `ctl00$cphBody$hdnRegExp` when present (`^[0-9]{6,6}$`). Continue is the LinkButton `__EVENTTARGET=ctl00$cphBody$btnContinue$lnkSubButton`. Live HTML encodes `__doPostBack` quotes as `'` / `'` — parsers must accept those or EVENTTARGET stays empty and the OTP form redisplays (HTTP 200, no `PostOtpAuth`).
3. Successful postback: **302 → `PersonalDetails.aspx`** (sets `PostOtpAuth` / portal auth). Not a cold `Login.aspx`. A cold `Login.aspx` GET without `PostOtpAuth` only sets `.ONLINEAUTH` and labs still redirects to login.

No JSON auth API was observed. This is ASP.NET WebForms end-to-end.

**Permanent-password road** (from a `login --browser --record` record, 2026-10-14, values never recorded): `GET /OnlineWeb/General/Login.aspx` is one form with `ctl00$cphBody$_loginView$tbUserId`, `tbUserName`, `tbPassword` (type=password), a BotDetect CAPTCHA (`LBD_VCID_c_general_login_ctl00_cphbody__loginview_captchalogin` hidden instance id, image at `/OnlineWeb/general/BotDetectCaptcha.ashx?get=image&c=…&t=…`, answer in `tbCaptchaLogin`), plus `__VIEWSTATE`/`__EVENTVALIDATION`; the page also offers `lbRegisterClientOTP` (the SMS road). The POST answers 302 → `/OnlineWeb/Services/FamilyHomePage.aspx`; the signed-in jar then holds `.ONLINEAUTH`, `ASP.NET_SessionId`, `HasOTP`, `TS…`, the Imperva `visid_incap_*`/`incap_ses_*` set and Glassbox `_cls_*`. The CAPTCHA is on this form too, so a password road cannot run unattended either — which is why `login --browser` hands the browser's sign-in over instead of replaying the form.

## Imperva

The site is fronted by Imperva. Headless datacenter clients often receive **Error 16**. This package:

- Does **not** bypass Imperva
- Does **not** solve CAPTCHA
- Expects a human on a residential / normal user machine

## Browser login (`login`)

`clalit-mcp login` opens a **loopback** page (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/`) for Israeli ID, CAPTCHA, and SMS OTP. The CAPTCHA image is fetched with the login cookie jar and shown in the page when possible. Writes `session.json`. Does **not** bypass Imperva or solve CAPTCHA. `--http` is accepted as a no-op alias.

Form posts use **303 See Other** (PRG) so Refresh / double-Continue cannot replay a CAPTCHA or OTP POST into a cleared waiter. Answers are buffered if Continue races ahead of the portal prompt. Only one `login` may run at a time (lockfile). Loopback session budget: **~30 minutes**.

After CAPTCHA Continue, the client POSTs to Clalit, follows redirects (or GETs the OTP page), and must reach SMS OTP **or** surface a clear error within **~30 seconds** (transport abort + captcha-check budget). Waiting pages auto-refresh every 2s so OTP / failure UI appears without a manual reload.

## Your own browser, handed over (`login --browser`)

`clalit-mcp login --browser` opens Chrome (or Chromium / Edge; `CHROME_PATH` picks one) on a profile of its own, `browser-profile/` under the config directory, at the portal's own sign-in page, and waits. You sign in there by whichever road Clalit Online gives you — the **permanent password**, or the SMS code — and type the CAPTCHA as on any visit. The CLI watches only which page the browser is on (host, path, and the names and types of the inputs on it; never their values). When a portal page past the sign-in is showing for two polls in a row — or you press Enter in the terminal — it reads the browser's cookies for `clalit.co.il`, imports them into a fresh jar, and checks them with **one** request for `LabsTestList.aspx`: only a 200 that is not a login page is accepted (a redirect anywhere, a bot challenge, or a jar without Imperva cookies fails closed with `BROWSER_SESSION_INCOMPLETE` and nothing is written). On success it writes `session.json` as the loopback login does, with the browser's user agent kept in it so later requests look like the same client; `connect()` sends that user agent from then on.

Nothing is typed into the site for you, and nothing is solved or bypassed: the browser did the sign-in, exactly as it would without the CLI. It is the same handover the Playwright cookie warm already does for the Imperva cookies before the loopback login, taken to its end — which is what makes the permanent-password road usable from the CLI without replaying the password form. Needs Node 22+ (its `WebSocket`); drives the browser over the DevTools Protocol with no automation flag, so the browser is the ordinary one. The window is closed once the session is saved (or the sign-in gave up), and on Ctrl-C; `--keep-open` leaves it open instead — the CLI lets go of it and exits as usual, and you close the window yourself.

`--record` additionally writes `login-record-<time>.json` (mode `0600`) in the config directory: every portal request the browser made during the sign-in (documents, XHR/fetch, form posts, the CAPTCHA image), reduced to shapes — method, path, query **keys** with each value's class and length (`digits(9)`, `alnum(8)`, `base64(2316)`), form **field names** with the same, a few request headers (the referer as a path), status, redirect paths, `Set-Cookie` **names**, and for each HTML page its forms, inputs (name, type, value shape), `__doPostBack` targets, script-set cookie **names**, redirects and sign-in links. Then the cookie names, domains and flags the browser ended with, and the path landed on. No value of yours is in it. It is what someone needs to build a sign-in that needs no browser, and it is safe to share.

## Debugging a reader

`CLALIT_DEBUG_DIR=/some/private/dir` makes the transport write every response body it receives there (`001_GET_200_Services_Labs_LabsTestList.aspx.html`, …; mode 0600; never headers or cookies), so a parser can be checked against what the portal actually answered. The files hold the member's record: keep the directory private and delete it afterwards.

Config directory (mode `0700`), resolved as:

1. `CLALIT_CONFIG_DIR` if set
2. `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/clalit-mcp`
3. `~/.config/clalit-mcp`

Files:

| File | Contents | Mode |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `session.json` | Serialized cookie jar + `authenticatedAt` (+ `userAgent` after `login --browser`) | `0600` |
| `browser-profile/` | The browser profile `login --browser` opens (the browser's own cookie store, encrypted by the browser as usual) | `0700` |
| `login-record-*.json` | `login --browser --record`: the sign-in's request **shapes** — paths, query keys, field names, value classes and lengths, cookie **names** (never a value) | `0600` |

| `otp-redisplay-*.json` | When OTP POST returns 200 still showing the form: posted **field names**, `__EVENTTARGET` used, and (v2) a redacted `otpPost` summary: page kind, presence flags, missing/unexpected keys, source page, digit-stripped validation text, cookie **names** before/after, timings (never OTP/ID/cookie/viewstate values) | `0600` |

Never log cookie values. Never commit this directory.

## Session completeness (fail-closed)

After SMS OTP, login **does not** write `session.json` unless:

1. The cookie jar contains at least one Imperva/TS-style name (`visid_incap_*`, `incap_ses_*`, `TS…`, or `_cls_*`), and
2. A probe of `LabsTestList.aspx` does **not** 302/HTML-redirect to Login.

A redacted `login-hops-*.json` dump (per-hop URL, status, content-type, Location path, page kind, Set-Cookie **names**, jar **names**, final count) is written under the config directory — never cookie values.

### Reading a failed-login dump

Start with `why.why` in the newest `login-hops-*.json`. The same reason code is on the `login` error page and in the stderr `[clalit login] why:` line.

- `otp_redisplayed_with_error`: the portal showed the OTP form again with a visible error. See `otpPost.validationSnippets[].text` (digits shown as `#`). This is usually a wrong or expired code, so request a new SMS.
- `otp_redisplayed_silent`: the form came back with no visible error. Compare `otpPost.post.missingExpectedKeys` with `otpPost.responseForm`.
- `otp_source_not_otp_form`: the OTP POST was built from a page without the SMS input. `otpPost.source.path` and `otpPost.source.presence` show which page. `otpPost.post.unexpectedLoginKeys` lists login or CAPTCHA keys that leaked into the POST.
- `otp_post_form_action_mismatch`: the page's `<form action>` differs from the POST URL.
- `otp_event_target_empty`: the POST had an empty `__EVENTTARGET`, so Continue never registered as clicked.
- `missing_post_otp_auth`: the client left the OTP form, but no `PostOtpAuth` or `AfterLogin` cookie arrived. See `hops[].pageKind`, `locationPath`, and `setCookieNames`.
- `missing_portal_defense_cookies`: no Imperva or TS defense cookies were found.
- `labs_login_redirect`: auth cookies arrived, but labs still redirects to sign-in.

`why.signals` adds hints such as `otp_entry_slow`, meaning more than 3 minutes passed between the OTP page and the code. `relatedDumps` links the matching `otp-redisplay-*.json`.

On a residential machine, login may optionally warm those defense cookies via **Playwright** (Chrome channel when available) before the Node CAPTCHA/OTP chain, then merges `Domain=.clalit.co.il` cookies into the tough-cookie jar with `loose` parsing. Playwright is a **devDependency** only (`npm install` in this repo). Login works without it; when Playwright is missing, the warm step is skipped.


## Idle TTL

Portal session TTL was **not measured** in live validation. Default soft idle hint: **~30 minutes**. Longer idle → expect `REAUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED` and run `login` again.

## Keep-alive

`GET /OnlineWeb/ServicesForAll/RefreshSession.aspx` was observed returning small HTML. Optional CLI: `clalit-mcp refresh-session`. Use sparingly; it does not replace login and must not be used to probe Imperva.

## Owner scope

The portal HTML may include family slider fields (`FamilySliderControl21$au` / `$cu`). The client **never** posts a member switch. Detail refs must come from the owner's own `LabsTestList.aspx` links only.

# Hosting one long-lived copy

Run locally, the session lives only as long as your MCP client keeps the server running. To keep one session alive across days and share it between several clients, run a single copy of the stdio server on an always-on machine at home and put a stdio-to-HTTP MCP proxy in front of it.

Assume none of this is reachable from the internet. Keep it on your home network or a private VPN.

```
MCP clients ──Bearer token──► MCP proxy ──stdio──► clalit-mcp   (one process, started once)
browser ──your own sign-in──► reverse proxy ──► clalit-mcp sign-in page (CLALIT_LOGIN_PORT)
```

## The proxy

Any proxy that starts the stdio server once and shares that one process between clients works, for example [TBXark/mcp-proxy](https://github.com/TBXark/mcp-proxy). Give each client its own bearer token so you can cut one off without touching the others:

```json
{
  "mcpProxy": { "addr": ":9090", "name": "mcp-proxy", "type": "streamable-http" },
  "mcpServers": {
    "clalit": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["tsx", "packages/cli/src/main.ts", "mcp"],
      "env": {
        "CLALIT_CONFIG_DIR": "/data/clalit",
        "CLALIT_LOGIN_HOST": "0.0.0.0",
        "CLALIT_LOGIN_URL": "https://mcp.example.com/clalit/login/"
      },
      "options": { "authTokens": ["<random token for client A>", "<random token for client B>"] }
    }
  }
}
```

Run the proxy from the repository root (or set the working directory), on a residential connection: Clalit turns datacenter IPs away.

## The sign-in page

With `CLALIT_LOGIN_URL` set, the page starts with the server and every "please sign in" answer links to that URL. Route it through a reverse proxy that puts your own sign-in in front (for example forward authentication), either at the root of a host name or under a path. Its links and forms are relative, so under a path, strip the prefix in the reverse proxy and give `CLALIT_LOGIN_URL` with the trailing slash (`https://mcp.example.com/clalit/login/`).

Inside a container, `CLALIT_LOGIN_HOST=0.0.0.0` lets the reverse proxy reach it; don't publish that port anywhere else.

## Clients and accounts

The bearer tokens decide who may call the tools. The Clalit session decides whose records they read. There is no link between the two: every token holder reads the account that last signed in on the page. Removing a token cuts that client off without signing anyone out of Clalit, and no client ever holds Clalit credentials.

For a second person, run a second copy with its own `CLALIT_CONFIG_DIR`, its own tokens and its own sign-in host, limited to them. The stdio server cannot tell which client is calling, so one copy per account is also what keeps one account's records out of another's session.

## Image

This repository publishes no container image. To run the stdio server in a container, build one from a Node 22 image with the packages installed and Playwright's Chromium for the sign-in page (`npx playwright install --with-deps chromium`), run it with `docker run -i`, and set `CLALIT_LOGIN_HOST=0.0.0.0` behind your proxy as above.

# Live verify (residential machine)

Datacenter and cloud IPs typically cannot complete Clalit login (Imperva Error 16). First live proof must happen on a residential or normal user network.

## Checklist

1. Clone `https://github.com/netanelavr/clalit-mcp`, `npm install`, `npm test` (all offline tests green).
2. On your own machine (home/residential network, normal browser already works for Clalit):
   ```sh
   npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts login
   ```
   A loopback browser page opens for Israeli ID, CAPTCHA (image from the portal session), and SMS OTP.
3. Enter Israeli ID, type the CAPTCHA shown in the page (not solved automatically), then the SMS OTP.
4. Confirm session file exists: `~/.config/clalit-mcp/session.json` (mode `0600`).
5. Run:
   ```sh
   npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts labs --json | head
   ```
6. Pick one `ref`, fetch detail and PDF:
   ```sh
   npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts lab --ref '…' --json
   npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts lab-document --ref '…' --out /tmp/clalit-lab.pdf
   file /tmp/clalit-lab.pdf   # expect PDF
   ```
7. If HTML shape differs from fixtures, save a **sanitized** HTML sample (strip names/IDs/values) and open a PR to adjust parsers.
8. Delete `/tmp/clalit-lab.pdf` when done. Never commit it.

## Blockers to expect

| Symptom | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Imperva Error 16 / `BOT_CHALLENGE` | Wrong network or automation fingerprint — use a residential network, no VPN datacenter. `login` does **not** bypass Imperva |
| Stuck on **Checking CAPTCHA…** / `CAPTCHA_CHECK_TIMEOUT` / `TIMEOUT` | Portal POST hung or CAPTCHA rejected; UI should error within ~30s and auto-refresh. Retry `login` |
| `CAPTCHA_REJECTED` / `OTP_PAGE_MISSING` | Wrong CAPTCHA or unexpected portal HTML — refresh image and retry. On reject, check `~/.config/clalit-mcp/captcha-rejected-*.json` (redacted field/POST keys) |
| `REAUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED` | Idle/session expired — `login` again |
| Empty labs list | Account has no rows in range, or date filter format mismatch |
| `NO_DOCUMENT` / `NOT_PDF` | Portal control id differs — capture sanitized detail HTML |

## HAR hygiene

If you capture a new HAR for מרשמים / הפניות:

- Redact cookies, tokens, IDs, phone numbers, clinical values
- Keep only path + field **names** (update [API-SOURCES.md](API-SOURCES.md) if you extract a map)
- Delete the raw HAR from disk after extracting the map
- Never commit `*.har`

# MCP

`npx tsx packages/cli/src/main.ts mcp` runs the stdio server. Client setup is in the [README](../README.md#mcp).

## Tools

1. `list_labs`: optional `fromDate` / `toDate`
2. `get_lab_result`: required `ref` from `list_labs`
3. `get_lab_document`: required `ref`; returns a base64 PDF
4. `list_prescriptions`: optional `fromDate` / `toDate` / `includeExpired`
5. `get_prescription_issue_status`: medicine row keys + `sectionId` (read status only)
6. `list_lab_orders`: lab orders (הפניות לבדיקות מעבדה); not MedicalReferrals
7. `get_lab_order`: required `ref` from `list_lab_orders`; no PDF
8. `list_documents`: required `source` (`visit_summaries`, `hospital_summaries`, `medical_approvals`, `form17`), optional `fromDate` / `toDate`
9. `get_document`: required `ref` from `list_documents`; returns a base64 PDF
10. `list_records`: required `source` (`diagnoses`, `sensitivities`, `chronic_medications`, `medicines_purchased`, `medication_approvals`, `imaging_clinics`, `imaging_hospitals`, `imaging_external`, `hospital_visits`, `hospital_labs`, `referrals`, `appointments`, `recommendations`, `vaccinations`, `blood_type`), optional `fromDate` / `toDate`; rows keyed by the portal's Hebrew headers (the API-backed sources by the portal's field names)
11. `get_record_document`: required `ref` from `list_records` (imaging reports, referrals); returns a base64 PDF
12. `get_hospital_lab_result`: required `link` and the row's `hospital` (its `context.value`) from a `hospital_labs` row; the draw's analytes
13. `clalit_login`: the sign-in link, or the status when already signed in
14. `clalit_session_status`: `state` (`signed_in`, `signed_out`, `expired`), `signedInAt`, `endsAt`, `lastCheckedAt`, `lastError`, and `signInUrl` when not signed in
15. `clalit_logout`: forgets the saved session

## Sign-in page

The server starts a small page on `CLALIT_LOGIN_HOST:CLALIT_LOGIN_PORT` (default `127.0.0.1:8765`) the first time someone needs to sign in. The page:

- asks how long the session should last (1 hour, 6 hours, 12 hours, 1 day, 2 days, 1 week; default 1 day);
- then runs the same ID, CAPTCHA and SMS code steps as `login` in the CLI ([AUTH.md](AUTH.md));
- shows the session's state afterwards, with "Sign in again" and "Sign out".

It answers only to `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and the host in `CLALIT_LOGIN_URL`, and every form carries a per-process token, so another website cannot drive it from your browser. Anyone who can open the page can sign in or out, so keep it on loopback, or behind your own authentication when hosted ([HOSTING.md](HOSTING.md)).

A session made with the CLI (`login` or `login --browser`) is picked up too: the server and the CLI share the session file.

## Keep-alive

Clalit has no refresh token: a sign-in gives a cookie session that the portal drops after roughly ten minutes without a request. While signed in, the server:

- requests `RefreshSession.aspx` every 4 minutes (the page the portal's own pages load in a hidden frame);
- checks every 20 minutes that a signed-in page still opens;
- saves the cookies after each round, so a restart picks the session back up;
- signs out when the chosen length runs out, and reports `expired` when Clalit ends the session sooner.

A network error keeps the session and retries on the next round. If another copy of the server or the CLI signs in, the next tool call picks that session up from the file.
